newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Aug 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Aug 5.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Tuesday:
* The most essential goods -- foods for grocery stores and medicine supplies for hospitals -- appeared to be getting to their destinations despite the UPS Teamsters strike.
* General Motors said it would buy back $2.5 billion in stock.
* The Dow Jones Industrial average rose modestly on Monday, although bonds continued to slide.
* U.S. construction spending fell 1.1 percent in June.
* The IMF recommended the U.S. Federal Reserve raise short-term interest rates.
* Russia's president Boris Yeltsin redenominated the ruble.
* MCI and Progressive Networks, an internet software company, are expected to announce a new video broadcasting service.
* Thailand moved closed to the completion of an international rescue package with an IMF.
* Creditors of Kia Group agreed to give the company two more months to settle its debts.
* The budget bill awaiting President Clinton's signature includes two new health insurance options.
* Polo Ralph Lauren shares have declined since their IPO amid investor caution on the retail industry.
* News Corp will take a $270 million charge to restructure HarperCollins.
* Corporate Japan is under new pressure to rid itself of scandal.
* Smoke shops hope that a stricter tobacco climate will boost the demand for speciality tobacco retailing.
